The solution works as follows:

1. Count the frequency of each character in the string
2. Find the maximum frequency - characters that appear this many times will be the last ones removed in the final operation
3. Traverse the string in reverse order
4. For each character, if its current count equals the maximum frequency, it means this is the last occurrence of this character in the string (when traversing backwards), so we include it in our result
5. Decrement the count as we process each character
6. Reverse the result since we built it backwards

This ensures we capture the string state right before the last operation, which removes one occurrence of each alphabet character that still exists.
